result.title: Raptor: Rejection-aware Adaptive Tree based on Speculative Decoding
result.summary: Tree-structured speculative decoding accelerates vision-language models (VLMs) by verifying multiple candidate continuations in parallel. However, long visual contexts increase the cost of speculative computation, making candidate coverage and redundant expansion important considerations beyond tree topology adaptation. We propose Raptor, a training-free framework that uses rejection feedback to jointly regulate candidate coverage and drafting effort. Our key insight is that acceptance length alone cannot distinguish insufficient candidate coverage from excessive deep expansion, and these conditions require different allocation decisions. Raptor therefore extracts complementary rejection-aware signals to characterize speculative progress, frontier coverage, and redundant expansion. These signals jointly guide bounded, momentum-smoothed updates of tree depth, branching width, and drafting budget, together with execution control that limits unnecessary drafting and progressively restores expansion when appropriate. Extensive experiments with two VLMs across seven multimodal benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of Raptor, achieving up to 2.39x average speedup over autoregressive decoding.

AI.brief_summary: Raptor 是一个免训练框架，用拒绝反馈提取「覆盖不足」与「过度扩张」两类互补信号，联合调节树状推测解码的深度、分支宽度与草稿预算，以加速长视觉上下文下的 VLM 解码。
AI.relevance_reason: 其用拒绝信号区分「候选覆盖不足」与「冗余扩张」并据此自适应分配计算、限制无效扩展的做法，可能与 LVR 中动态计算与停止/扩展决策的判据设计有概念联系，可供核查；但论文针对解码加速，不涉及推理期 latent 状态内容。
